call_points.text: Order book grew to ₹3,197 Cr, including the first-ever order from the US market.
Vadod Unit 4 received Power Grid approval for 400 kV transformers; commercial contribution from next financial year.
Raw material prices under pressure but pass-through via price variation clause; margins expected to sustain at 17-18%.
Export target of 15% of revenue over next three years; no export revenue in Q1FY27.
CRGO steel anti-dumping inquiry initiated; no short-term impact expected, verdict by March 2027.
Chinese players allowed in PSU tenders; no material impact observed yet, monitoring closely.
Management reiterated target of 40% revenue CAGR for 3 years with stable margins.
Targeting exports to reach 15% of total revenue within the next 3 years.
Vadod utilization targeted at 65% in FY27 and 100% in FY28.
INR 180 Cr capex planned for tank/radiator unit (₹170-180 Cr) and IDT unit (₹65 Cr).
FY26 order wins stood at ₹2,507 Cr, elevating ending order book to ₹2,493 Cr.
75% of current order book is covered by price variation clauses (PVC).

operating_notes.text: Secured ₹190.00 Cr order from RVPN for 53 units of 50 MVA 132/33 KV Power Transformers and NIFPES systems.
Total MVA produced in FY26 across 5 manufacturing units was 22,943 MVAs.
Unit 4 (Vadod) operated at ~39% capacity utilization in FY26 and is targeted at 65% in FY27.
PGCIL approval received on April 2, 2026, for transformer manufacturing up to 400kV at Vadod unit.
Received LOA for ₹285.15 Cr from PSTCL for 23 Nos. 160 MVA, 220/66 kV Power Transformers, NIFPES, and optional spares.
Order book of ₹3,116.63 Cr as of 30 June 2026; ~₹2,400 Cr executable in FY27.
220 kV class transformers account for over 55% of order book; 400 kV and reactors contribute ~₹275 Cr.
Sales-based capacity utilization of 4,381 MVA in Q1FY27 against installed capacity of 63,060 MVA.
H1FY27 raw material costs stood at ₹718.83 Cr, representing 83.9% of revenue.
Inventories increased by ₹268.8 Cr during H1FY27, significantly impacting cash generation.
Secured first order from the United States in Q2FY27.
Top 10 suppliers contributed to 66.13% of raw materials purchased.
Manufacturing capacity utilization reached 98.28% in FY26.
AE Components approved ₹193.58 Cr backward integration capex for transformer tanks, frames, and radiators to be completed in one year.

timeline.summary: On May 2, 2026, Atlanta Electricals secured a ₹190 Cr order from RVPN for 53 power transformers and NIFPES systems.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹747.62 Cr, net profit ₹102.19 Cr.
Atlanta Electricals Limited’s **Tejalben Saunakkumar Panchal** shared Q4FY26 earnings call audio (11 May 2026) on the company website.
Atlanta Electricals received a 2-year debarment order from SBPDCL concerning a FY24 transformer supply order.
Atlanta Electricals conducted its Q4FY26 earnings call, confirming complete term debt elimination and outlining growth plans for 400kV/765kV transformers.
Atlanta Electricals received a ₹285.15 Cr Letter of Award from PSTCL for 23 power transformers and NIFPES.
Atlanta Electricals held its Q1FY27 earnings call on 22 July 2026, reporting 48% YoY revenue growth to ₹466.33 Cr and a record order book of ₹3,116.63 Cr.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹390.08 Cr, net profit ₹32.12 Cr.
Atlanta Electricals reported Q2FY27 revenue of ₹390.1 Cr and a record order book of ₹3,197 Cr, including its first US order.
AE Components approved ₹193.58 Cr capex for a captive transformer tank, frame, and radiator facility targeted within one year.
